title: EU Hosted Workflow Automation: Best Platforms 2026
summary: EU hosted workflow automation stores your workflows and credentials exclusively in EU data centres. Compare platforms offering this feature.
body_markdown:
## Where Activepieces fits for EU data requirements


Activepieces meets an EU residency requirement in two ways: its managed cloud can be pinned to an EU or US region and carries SOC 2 Type II, or you self-host the MIT-licensed core.


In both cases you still have to check the connected apps and support access yourself.


The engine and the stored run data are the part it can put in your hands.


### Managed cloud in an EU region


On the managed cloud you pick an EU or US region, so the workflow engine and the stored run data sit where you chose. That settles two of the four things this article keeps separating. It doesn't settle the other two.


Activepieces has 741 integrations, and each one you add, such as a spreadsheet action like Insert Row or Find Rows, talks to a third-party app, so if any of those 741 vendors changes their API, your workflow could break.


Where that app keeps its data is the app vendor's decision, not the region you selected in Activepieces.


Look at the integration selector in the flow builder and the problem is plain: Google Sheets, Microsoft Excel 365, AITable and Retable sit side by side, and each of those is a separate vendor with its own hosting.


Choosing an integration is a residency decision, so read the catalogue that way and not as a count of logos.


### Self-host or air-gap


If the requirement is that data never leaves your network, self-hosting is the answer, and air-gapping goes further by cutting the instance off from the outside entirely.


Then the engine, the run data and the support access are all yours, because nobody at the vendor has a path in unless you build one.


You pay in operations: your team patches, backs up and upgrades the instance. A regulated team, in healthcare for instance, can self-host to keep data in its own environment, but I wouldn't read that as a certification claim, because none is made here.


### Controls around the data


Region is only half a review, and the other half stalls when a security team has to take a vendor's maturity on trust.


Activepieces has an MIT-licensed core, so a reviewer can clone the repository and inspect the code before deploying it with Docker, Compose or Kubernetes, or running it air-gapped. On top of that sit SSO and SCIM, custom role-based access control and audit logs.


In practice that means you can provision and remove people from your identity provider, limit who can edit flows that touch personal data, and trace who changed what afterwards.


It's not the fit if you need a HIPAA BAA or an ISO certificate, since neither is among the facts I can point to.


If you can't spare anyone to run a self-hosted instance and the managed regions don't match your rules, it's also the wrong tool.


For the security documents and enterprise pricing, go to[the sales page](https://www.activepieces.com/sales) .


Activepieces is the better fit for EU teams that decide a data-residency review by inspecting the system itself rather than trusting a vendor's statement.


Its MIT-licensed core lets a reviewer clone the repository, read the queue and worker architecture, and run it self-hosted or fully air-gapped before signing off, while the managed cloud can be pinned to an EU region for those who prefer not to operate it.


That evidence covers the engine and the stored run data, and the connected apps and support access still need separate checks under either option.
